headline: High: shared filesystem plus broad egress makes Mentat→Perplexity data leakage and unverified-output cascades plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat can read/write the filesystem and shares state via filesystem, while Perplexity can browse and ingest uploaded documents. If Mentat writes attacker-controlled text into files that Perplexity later reads or summarizes, prompt injection is plausible. The bridge is not direct by default, so this is below high.
conditions: IF Mentat writes untrusted content into a file that Perplexity later uploads or reads
IF Perplexity treats file contents as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories
Rename shared files to clearly mark them untrusted
Disable Perplexity uploads for files produced by Mentat
Review Perplexity outputs before acting on them

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat can read selected files and has broad network egress; Perplexity uploads documents and sends queries to vendor APIs. If the same workspace contains secrets or sensitive source code, Mentat can expose them into files that Perplexity then uploads, creating a realistic exfiltration path. The pair is not isolated by default, so the blast radius can include sensitive data.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace
IF Mentat places those contents into a file or prompt that Perplexity uploads or queries
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Use a separate non-sensitive folder for Perplexity inputs
Turn off document upload for sensitive tasks
Redact files before handing them to Perplexity
requires-engineering: add workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write files and modify git state, while Perplexity cannot write locally but can browse and process uploaded files. There is no direct write-write conflict, yet both can touch the same project artifacts through the filesystem, so concurrent edits or stale reads can corrupt work. The conflict is real in default multi-instance use, but not as severe as unrestricted dual writers.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or document set
IF Mentat commits or rewrites files while Perplexity is analyzing an older copy
mitigations: Pause one agent while the other edits
Use separate branches for Mentat work
Export Perplexity inputs as read-only snapshots
Check git status before applying Mentat diffs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is a search-RAG agent that produces cited answers, and Mentat is a coding assistant that can turn those outputs into file edits. If Mentat treats Perplexity's answer as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code changes or commits. The pathway exists in normal use, but Mentat's diff-based confirmation reduces severity below high.
conditions: IF Mentat uses Perplexity output as a factual source for edits
IF Mentat applies diffs without independent verification of the cited claims
mitigations: Require a human review of Perplexity claims before editing
Cross-check cited sources in the browser
Limit Mentat to small diffs per task
Ask Perplexity for primary sources, not summaries

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat handles source code and model-provider API keys, while Perplexity processes uploaded documents and browsing context through vendor-hosted services. If regulated or confidential material is uploaded to Perplexity, retention and residency obligations may differ from local Mentat handling. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are uploaded to Perplexity
IF the operator expects local-only handling or a stricter retention policy than Perplexity provides
mitigations: Do not upload regulated data to Perplexity
Strip secrets from files before upload
Use Mentat locally for sensitive code changes
Review vendor retention settings before use
requires-engineering: route regulated workloads to a compliant environment
